title: TVI-CoT: Text-Visual Interleaved Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Multimodal Understanding
claim: A model alternates between text reasoning and selecting visual features, attending to different image regions at each step until it answers.
layout: Single wide diagram, bottom-to-top inputs to LLM to outputs, zoom inset bottom-right
description: A single wide diagram with a large yellow rounded box labeled 'Large Language Model (LLM)' in the middle. Below it, an image of a cyclic quadrilateral goes through a blue 'Vision Encoder' to a row of blue visual-feature squares. A question text goes through a green 'Tokenizer' to a row of green text-feature squares. Both feature rows feed into the LLM. Above the LLM, arrows lead to a sequence of outputs, left to right: gray text boxes for textual reasoning steps 1 and 2, each with a red <Think> token, and visual reasoning steps 1 and 2. The visual steps show a red <Look> token with blue squares and a 'Select visual features' box. The sequence ends with a red <Answer> A. A dashed inset at bottom right shows the cropped geometry regions attended to at the 1st and 2nd reasoning steps.
caption: Overview of the TVI-CoT framework. Given an image and a question, the vision encoder and tokenizer produce visual and text features that are fed into the LLM. The model dynamically alternates between textual reasoning steps ($\langleThink\rangle$), which perform chain-of-thought analysis, and visual reasoning steps ($\langleLook\rangle$), which select relevant visual features from the image. Each visual reasoning step attends to different image areas conditioned on the current reasoning state (e.g., the 1st step focuses on $\angle A$ while the 2nd step shifts to $\angle C$). This interleaving continues adaptively until the model produces $\langleAnswer\rangle$.
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has proven effective for enhancing problem-solving in large language models. However, when applied to multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), existing CoT approaches suffer from a fundamental limitation: they perform reasoning entirely in text without accessing visual features during the reasoning process. After initial visual encoding, image information becomes inaccessible, forcing models to reason based solely on whatever was captured in the initial description, which forms a `vision-blind reasoning' paradigm that limits fine-grained visual extraction, error verification, and adaptive attention. We propose Text-Visual Interleaved Chain-of-Thought (TVI-CoT), a framework that enables explicit interleaving of textual reasoning and visual feature access through learnable control tokens <THINK>, <LOOK> and <ANSWER>. These tokens allow dynamic switching between reasoning and visual grounding, attending to relevant image regions conditioned on the evolving reasoning state. Experiments on eight benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art results among MLLM-based CoT methods and notable performance boost compared to the baseline: +6.1% on MMMU, +3.8% on MathVerse, +3.4% on MathVista, and +3.4% on ScienceQA. Code is available at https://github.com/hulianyuyy/TVI-CoT.
